title: Now We See in a Mirror Dimly
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: What we see of Christ now is real, just not complete. We live by faith, not sight, until the day we see him face to face.
exhortation: One of the great ironies of this world is how much of it rests on what we can see. Seeing is believing. When you hear about a tragedy secondhand, you may think it's terrible, but it's different when you see it. Watch the video, and suddenly it's real. Most of our life is lived by sight.

But we live in a time when we can't live by sight. If we do, we'll go spiritually astray and build our lives on all the wrong things, because what we see now is partial and imperfect at best. Looking at the world now is like looking at the sun reflected in a lake: a glimmer, not the real thing.

That's the bad news. The good news is that when we look into God's word, when we read of the glories of Christ in the Gospels, see them unfolded in the letters of Paul and the other apostles, and trace the Old Testament as it points toward Jesus, what we see is real. It just isn't complete. It's the real thing, but it's fuzzy. That's why we need faith. We walk by faith, not by sight, trusting that the day is coming when we will see with redeemed, perfected eyes, not a reflection but the full face of the sun, with eyes that can withstand the blaze.

On that day we will experience something we can't fathom now. We will know fully, even as we have been fully known and loved. We'll understand the glories of Christ crucified and the depths of his suffering, things we think we understand now but don't fully. We'll see the glory he shared with the Father in eternity past and understand what he gave up when he became a man. We barely grasp these things now, but one day we will see them with unveiled faces. So, Christian, have faith today. Look into that dim mirror with me at the glories of Christ. Behold what you can, glory in what has been revealed, and rejoice in the God of our salvation. The day is coming soon when we will see in full.
prayer: Lord, what you have for us is beyond our imagination and understanding, secure and hidden in heaven with you, where moth and rust cannot destroy. Help us not to put our investments in this world, where they will be destroyed, but to set our treasure in heaven, in you, Jesus. One day you will come and split the clouds. You will come in justice, right every wrong and dry every tear.

Fill us with faith. Give us eyes of faith to see the unseen and not put our hope in what is seen. We recognize that we can't do this in our own power, so we ask for the power and filling of your Holy Spirit to do this work in us and give us eyes of faith. In Jesus' name, amen.
